lines: One ship cost the world 9.6 billion dollars a day.
In March 2021, the Ever Given got stuck in the Suez Canal. It's 400 meters long, longer than the Eiffel Tower is tall.
It wedged itself sideways across the Suez Canal. For six days, nothing could pass.
By the time it floated free, more than 400 ships were waiting in line.
That's 9.6 billion dollars of goods, stuck every single day.
All because one narrow canal is the shortcut between Europe and Asia.
Follow for a new megaproject every day.
